desc:
Ad creative briefs for images and video give your designer, editor or creator clear written direction: the message, the hook, the layout and the words to use. Ecom Swift LLC writes the briefs so the first draft lands close to what you pictured.

## What is an ad creative brief?

An ad creative brief is a short document that tells a designer or video editor exactly what an ad must say, show and do. It names the product, the buyer, the main message, the visual style, the sizes needed and the action you want the viewer to take. It is the difference between "make something nice" and a task someone can finish properly.

Without a brief, creators guess. They guess your audience, your tone and which feature matters most, and each wrong guess costs a round of revisions. Those revisions cost time, delay your launch and often end with an ad that nobody loves.

## How a brief improves ad performance

Ads compete for a fraction of a second of attention. In that moment the viewer decides whether the ad is about them. A brief built on real buyer research puts the right problem, face or product in the first frame, which is where most people either stay or scroll away.

A brief also makes testing possible. When each ad is written to test one idea, such as price versus convenience, the results tell you something. When ads are made without a plan, a win or a loss teaches you nothing, because too many things changed at once.

## What a useful brief contains

- The single message each ad must communicate, in one sentence.
- A hook for the first few seconds of video, or the focal point of an image.
- A shot list for video, or a layout sketch in words for images.
- Sizes and formats for each placement, such as feed, stories, reels and search display.
- Headline and primary text suggestions, with a few options to test.
- The tone of voice, with sample phrases to use and phrases to avoid.
- Product details that must be shown accurately, such as colors, sizes and packaging.
- Reference examples, so the creator can see the style you mean.
- A call to action that matches the page the ad leads to.
- A checklist for reviewing the first draft and giving useful feedback.

## How we write briefs

We start by studying your product, your buyers and any past ads you have run, including the ones that disappointed. We look at what competitors show and which claims everyone repeats, so your ad can stand apart. If you have customer messages or questions, we read those as well, since buyers often describe their problem better than any marketer.

We then write the briefs in plain language. The Basic package gives you one brief for a single idea. Standard covers a set of briefs that mix images and short video, with several headline options each. Premium adds hooks for the opening seconds of video, sizes for every main placement, a suggested testing order and a feedback checklist. We write the direction only; the images and videos themselves are made by your designer or creator, though we can write scripts and review competitor ads as add-ons.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each ad one message and one action.
- Show the product in use within the first moments.
- Brief for sound-off viewing by adding clear on-screen text.
- Check every claim against what you can honestly deliver.
- Keep safe margins, so platform buttons do not cover key words.

**Avoid:**
- Cramming several offers into one ad.
- Briefing with vague words such as "premium" without examples.
- Using music, fonts or footage you do not have rights to use.
- Making claims about health or income that platforms restrict.
- Sending creators feedback as feelings instead of specific changes.

## Who it is for

This service suits a store owner who hires freelancers and keeps getting drafts that miss the point. It suits a founder who films their own videos but does not know what to say in the first seconds. It also suits a team working with an agency that wants to keep creative direction in-house.

## What we need and how to start

Send your website address, product photos or samples, a few lines about your ideal buyer and any past ads, good or bad. Tell us which creator or agency will read the brief, if you already have one. We may ask for view access to your ad account as a partner or team member to study past results, and we never need your passwords. We reply with a short question list and then deliver the briefs as a document you can forward directly.
